selector.rationale: The presence of a pruritic back rash with crusting erythematous plaques, positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay, and rapid plasma reagin testing titer of 1:64, along with the eye findings, strongly supports ocular syphilis as the most comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: HIV-related Retinitis
rejected.why: While the patient has HIV, the specific eye findings and positive syphilis tests point more directly to an ocular syphilis diagnosis.

rejected.label: HIV-related immunosuppression
rejected.why: This is a contributing factor but not a specific diagnosis for the eye condition described.

rejected.label: Syphilitic retinitis
rejected.why: This is a subtype of ocular syphilis and the broader diagnosis of ocular syphilis encompasses the retinitis and other findings.
